title: Preserve opening Galaxy subject through renderer reinitialization

scope.subject: Preserve the exact native fixed orbit anchor with the captured Galaxy pose when settings or renderer remount; ensure drag continues around the already visible subject.

research_summary: Exact current public No-query cold Galaxy keeps the physical Milky Way core centred under real drag. Source distinguishes returning camera pose from input ownership: the shared view snapshot carries position and quaternion but omits fixed orbit anchor, so renderer reinitialization for a normal quality change restores a free camera instead of the exact existing native fixed pivot. Preserve the original native fixed-point geometry in the existing snapshot. Reject blanket look-at or camera replacement; restoring the pose and anchor must not recenter, invent a star, or affect true free flight.

sources.finding: Current pinned native renderer remains the authority; no upstream patch or new camera.
The current R3F scene uses a shared React ref for repeatable camera restore on renderer replacement.
The existing native orbitPoint and saved-view ref already own pivot geometry and restoration; persist only the state needed by the same executor.
Use true move/down/up events and Three projection of the rendered galaxy, not semantic flags alone.

search_ladder.conclusion: Reuse the installed pinned MIT YEIS: the first visit already has a stable mathematical centre and only remount loses its state.
Keep current R3F camera and existing React ref snapshots; no second renderer or drag loop.
Keep native CameraController.orbitPoint, equivalent to saved target restoration already used by the same project; do not layer cinematic camera-controls into native Galaxy.
Preserve exact native local anchor, radius and label in existing snapshot; restore saved quaternion after establishing target, no new screen-space target heuristic.

candidates.name: Native fixed orbit point and existing Galaxy view snapshot
candidates.source: Exact main and loaded native CameraController
candidates.reason: Preserves the same astronomical subject and rendered orientation; leaves genuine free flight unchanged.

candidates.name: Install separate Drei camera-controls on the already native Galaxy
candidates.reason: Would create competing input and position owners and lose native floating-frame semantics.

decision.rationale: Retain and restore only the real native fixed orbit anchor when the saved pose was in orbit, restoring the original quaternion to avoid a snap.
decision.fallback: Do not publish if the public direct drag repro is not improved or first-view, free flight and renderer handoffs regress.
